extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/Principal investigators and institutional grants administrators preparing NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, formatting, and submitting NIH grant applications, including which instructions and forms to follow, page limits and text-field rules, use of submission systems, and coordination with institutional sponsored-projects staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: If any instructions differ, follow this hierarchy: NIH Guide notices have the highest priority. Notices of Policy Changes are incorporated into the NIH Grants Policy Statement (GPS) each year. Notices that modify a specific opportunity are listed in the Related Notices section of that opportunity. Specific instructions in your notice of funding opportunity are secondary. General instructions in the How to Apply – Application Guide are tertiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay special attention to policy notices posted in the NIH Guide after the most recent GPS update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow How to Apply – Application Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Apply provides comprehensive instructions for completing application forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this guide for comprehensive form instructions and quick links for registration, formatting attachments, page limits, rules for text fields, submission policies, and guidance if a federal system threatens on-time submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Forms Directory / correct forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Find reference copies of essential NIH forms, instructions, and format pages used to apply for, manage, and close out grant awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preview application forms and ensure you are using the correct, current form versions for your activity code and opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format attachments correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the guidance on formatting attachments used in NIH applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Format Attachments and related format pages for attachment-specific instructions and required formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe page limits specified for narrative sections and attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Page Limits guidance for limits on specific attachments and narrative sections; exceeding limits can affect reviewers' ability to evaluate the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow rules for text fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with NIH rules for text fields (character/word limits, allowable content, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules for Text Fields for constraints and formatting expectations for online text fields versus attached documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register and preview application forms (system readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete required registrations and preview application forms before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use registration resources and preview forms to ensure all required registrations (eRA Commons, Grants.gov, institution accounts) and form fields are in order well before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ASSIST or designated preparation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ASSIST (or other NIH-recommended tools) to prepare your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the guidance on 'Using ASSIST to Prepare Your Application' to assemble forms and attachments correctly and catch common assembly issues prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize time to complete the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and organize your schedule to complete all parts of the application on time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult 'Organize Your Time to Complete the Application' to allocate adequate time for drafting, internal review, and institutional sign-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce a well-written, well-formatted narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-written, well-formatted application is key to success; narrative sections should clearly communicate research intent and value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'General Grant Writing Tips' and 'Communicating Research Intent and Value' to craft concise, clear narratives; choose the approaches you consider optimal for your unique application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow advice on specific application sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use section-specific guidance for narrative attachments such as the Research/Program Plan, Specific Aims, Budget, and Biographical Sketches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Advice on Application Sections' for targeted writing guidance for Research Plan, Specific Aims, Budget, Biographical Sketches, and other attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sample applications and annotated form sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult sample grant applications, attachment format examples, sample language, and annotated form sets to learn how others presented their ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Samples page provides examples that can help shape structure, language, and formatting choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission policies and contingency guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to NIH submission policies and follow guidance if a federal system issue threatens on-time submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review 'Submission Policies' and 'Dealing with System Issues' for procedures on late submissions, system failures, and applicable exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with your institutional Office of Sponsored Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete any institutional final steps and notify the appropriate sponsored-projects staff so they can finalize and submit the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once your application is ready, let your institution's Office of Sponsored Programs know it is time to finalize and submit; follow your organization's internal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NIH or institutional staff when unsure
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct questions to your organization's sponsored programs office or NIH contacts if you need assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided contact links and resources (Need Help?) before submission to resolve uncertainties about instructions, forms, or policies.
